sections.overview: Pseudantechinus macdonnellensis is a small marsupial of arid central Australia.
sections.identification: Its short, thick-based tail stores fat. Unlike P. bilarni, it is not described as having a proportionally long, slender tail. It is also distinct in current taxonomies from P. woolleyae, recognized separately in 1988.
sections.habitat: It shelters among rocks and termite mounds in arid landscapes.
sections.diet: It eats termites, beetles, grasshoppers and other invertebrates.
sections.behavior: It is mainly nocturnal; winter basking and daily torpor are also reported.
sections.reproduction: Females usually breed annually and carry five or six young in the pouch.
sections.ecology: A 2017 genetic study proposed synonymizing P. roryi with P. macdonnellensis after finding the sampled specimens indistinguishable. The Mammal Diversity Database now includes roryi here; see P. roryi.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database lists it as Least Concern globally.
